title: Blood Flow Imaging with Ultrafast Doppler
protocol: Connect the peristaltic pump, the blood mimicking fluid reservoir, the pulse dampener and the Doppler flow phantom with plastic tubes.
Choose the canal with a 4 mm diameter.
Program the pump to eject 720 mL/min of fluid for 0.3 s and then to eject 50 mL/min for 0.7 s.
Run the pump and gently shake the pipes to expel potential air bubbles.
Connect the ultrafast-enabled research scanner to the host computer with the PCI express link.
Change the transducer adapter on the ultrasound scanner to match the probe connector, then connect the probe.
Run Matlab and activate the ultrasound scanner license.
Design a conventional focused “B-Mode” sequence for probe positioning.
Set the imaging depth to 50 mm.
Set the focal depth to 35 mm.
Design an ultrafast ultrasound sequence.
Set the imaging depth to 50 mm.
Program 3 tilted plane-waves at [-3,0,3] degree.
Set the pulse repetition frequency to 12 kHz.
Use 4 half-cycles for the ultrasound waveform.
Assume a center frequency of 5.2 MHz.
Set the total duration to 1 second.
Apply ultrasound gel on the probe’s lens.
Place the probe on the phantom and launch the B-Mode ultrasound sequence.
Locate the canal of interest.
Position the probe in longitudinal view.
Maintain the probe manually at the position of interest.
End the B-Mode sequence and start the ultrafast sequence acquisition script.
Save the raw data (Radio-Frequency data, "RF").
Launch the image reconstruction script using the default software.
Create an IQ data matrix after processing.
Filter clutter using a Matlab script.
Reshape the 3D IQ matrix into a 2D Casorati matrix, named IQr.
Compute the singular value decomposition of IQr.
Compute the Spatial Similarity Matrix C using spatial singular vectors U.
Identify blood subspace boundaries N.
Filter the IQ data using cutoff N.
Compute power Doppler map PD by integrating the envelope of filtered data IQt along the temporal dimension.
Display the PD map in logarithmic scale.
Set the dynamic range, compute the mean PD outside the canal and use this value in dB as the lower bound of the dynamic range.
Define a circular region of interest (ROI) containing 1 to 30 pixels.
Average the IQf signal over the ROI pixels to obtain a vector of nt time points.
Compute the Doppler spectrogram using the square magnitude of the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT).
Set the STFT window to a 60-samples Hann window.
Set the STFT overlap to 90% of the window length.
Overlay the center frequency at each time point on the spectrogram.
Convert frequency f values into blood axial velocities vz using the Doppler formula.
